finalModelMessage:
I've confirmed the issue: this page's registration controls are not exposed with proper accessible roles or names — the "Register" text and the row icons (`img`) have no accessible role (button/link) or name that assistive technology (or role-based automation) can target. Both `button` and `link` role queries for "Register" time out because no such accessible element exists in the tree.

**Result: Registration could not be completed.**

**What stopped me:** On `/inaccessible`, the workshop table renders "Register" as plain, non-interactive text (and unlabeled `img` icons) rather than as a properly labeled button or link. There is no accessible element exposing the role/name "Register" that can be activated via role-based interaction, so I could not open the registration form for "Building Accessible Forms in Java" (or any other session) to proceed with filling in the attendee name, email, meal preference, or terms acceptance. This is itself a significant accessibility defect: keyboard and screen-reader users relying on the accessibility tree would be unable to register for any workshop on this page.
